title: Compact cross-encoder gating and canary scaling for multilingual rerank
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: introduce a compact cross-encoder variant and automated gating logic so we can reduce tail latency and cost for rerank while preserving multilingual parity. Deliver a canary + progressive scale strategy, a lightweight regression harness per locale, and circuit-breakers that fall back to the current baseline model on quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Compact cross-encoder (quantized FP16/INT8 path) is available behind the rerank endpoint as a candidate variant.
End-to-end median latency improvement >= 18% and 95th-percentile latency improvement >= 12% on the multi-locale benchmark compared to baseline for top-10 rerank requests.
No measurable quality regression: multilingual nDCG@10 drop <= 0.5 points vs baseline per locale; failing locales must be flagged and auto-rolled back.
Canary rollout automation that ramps QPS per locale and triggers rollback on latency or quality gates.
Regression harness runs as part of pre-rollout checks and daily smoke runs; math for thresholds and alerting configured in Console dashboards.
discussion: 2026-03-10 - Asha: Kicked off spike to evaluate compact 1. small cross-encoder (4-6M params pruning + int8) vs baseline (<100M) on EN/ES/JA split. Initial microbenchmarks show ~22% token-level throughput gain but differing nDCG impact by language.

2026-03-11 - Miguel: Lab results: EN/ES nDCG delta -0.2 and -0.4 respectively; JA shows -1.1 (unacceptable). Hypothesis: tokenization mismatch + subword coverage causing JA degradation. Suggested per-locale fallback gating.

2026-03-11 - Lina (NLP): Proposed a locale-aware gating rule: if locale-specific nDCG drop > 0.6 then route to baseline for that locale during canary. Also proposed augmenting training eval with synthetic transliterations for JA to reduce gap.

2026-03-12 - Miguel: Implemented preliminary canary controller that accepts per-locale weightings, QPS ramp schedule, and threshold hooks for latency and quality. Hooked tests into CI but still need stable daily harness infra.
decisions: Adopt compact cross-encoder variant as a first-class optional model variant behind rerank; it will be referred to as 'ce-compact-v1'.
Use per-locale gating: traffic allocation is controlled per-region/locale. Locale-level gate evaluation uses the regression harness nDCG metrics and production sampling QA metrics.
Rollouts will follow canary -> regional ramp -> global ramp pattern with automatic rollback on predefined gates (latency or nDCG).
Quality gate thresholds: nDCG@10 drop across 3 consecutive daily runs > 0.6 triggers rollback; 95p latency increase > 15% triggers rollback.
implementation_notes: Model artifact: store ce-compact-v1 under model-catalog with tags [compact, int8, multilingual-candidate].
Runtime changes: add a lightweight routing flag 'rerank.model_variant' in the request path; controller resolves variant by locale and canary weight.
Batching/kernel selection: ensure compact variant uses optimized small-batch kernels to preserve latency; measure CPU vs GPU load to avoid host bottlenecks.
KV cache: compact variant currently does not share KV cache with baseline. Evaluate opportunity to reuse shared embeddings to reduce warm-up.
Metrics: emit per-request fields: model_variant, locale, rerank_time_ms, ddg_position_scores, n_candidates. Hook to Console traces and rollout dashboards.
Fallback: implement 'circuit breaker' that checks recent regressions and flips traffic to baseline for affected locale keys.
test_plan: Unit tests for routing logic, per-locale config parsing, and canary schedules (PR required).
Regression harness: add per-locale evaluation tuples derived from Prod-anchored test sets (EN/ES/JA/FR/DE/KO). The harness must produce nDCG@10, MRR, and precision@1 daily.
Smoke in staging: run a 1 hour canary with 5% QPS routed to ce-compact-v1 for all locales and verify latency, memory, and correctness via synthetic assertions.
Production sampling: route 0.5% of live traffic to candidate variant in 'monitor-only' mode for 24h to collect realistic signals before canary ramp.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary dry-run: deploy model in staging, run synthetic traffic, confirm perf and harness metrics. (owner: Miguel)
Phase 1 - Monitor-only: 0.5% prod sampling for 24h, collect metrics, run automated regression harness. (owner: SRE)
Phase 2 - Locale canary: For locales passing harness, start per-locale 5% QPS ramp over 6 hours. Evaluate gates after 24h.
Phase 3 - Regional ramp: Increase to 25% for regions that meet gates over 48h.
Phase 4 - Global ramp: 100% traffic for non-failing locales or fallback to baseline for failing ones. Full cutover only after 7 days of stable signals.
risks_and_mitigations: Quality regressions in morphologically complex languages (e.g., JA, KO): mitigate with per-locale gating and more robust eval sets, postpone rollouts by locale.
Increased 95p latency due to small-batch kernel inefficiencies: mitigate by tuning batching thresholds and offloading lightweight ops to CPU when beneficial.
Model artifact inconsistency between instances: validate checksums at deployment and enable automatic redeploy if mismatch detected.
Telemetry noise: set minimum sample thresholds before triggering rollbacks to avoid flapping on small-sample variance.
next_steps: Finish wiring regression harness to daily CI job and add locale partitions for JA/KO by 2026-03-15. (owner: Lina)
Complete integration tests for canary controller and merge PR. (owner: Miguel)
Prepare runbook entries for on-call to respond to locale rollback alerts. (owner: SRE)
Schedule stakeholder demo after first successful 5% locale canary. (owner: Asha)
